points.description: Says pandas and koalas are similar because both are specialists with a narrow or restricted diet, supported by the article (pandas eat almost only bamboo; koalas eat almost only eucalyptus leaves). Credit the word 'specialist' with a clear link to a restricted diet or habitat, or both diets named with the similarity drawn.
points.partial_credit: Half when the diet facts or the word 'specialist' are given without a clear similarity.

levels.says: Gives the diet facts for both animals, or says they are 'specialists', but does not clearly draw the similarity. Also give this level if only one animal's diet is given with a claim that they are alike.

points.description: Says pythons differ from both animals because they are generalists. They adapt to and survive in many environments or eat many things, and they thrive and spread (e.g., Everglades, or climates across about a third of the US). Do not credit 'pythons are bigger or dangerous' with no reference to adaptability.
points.partial_credit: Half for the spread or success fact without the link to adaptability or being a generalist.

levels.says: Gives an article fact about the pythons' spread or success (e.g., breeding in the Everglades) but does not say they are adaptable or generalists.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the specialist similarity for pandas and koalas, plus the contrast that pythons are adaptable generalists, using article details. Part marks are for facts without the link. Ignore the Invasive Species prompt.
rubric.answer_key: Similarity: both are specialists with very narrow diets (pandas eat almost only bamboo; koalas eat almost only eucalyptus leaves). Difference: pythons are generalists that adapt to many environments and thrive in changing conditions, as in the Everglades, where they are invasive. Pandas and koalas depend on stable conditions.

review_notes: P1 says to credit 'either the diet detail or the word specialist', so a student who gives only one animal's diet could get full marks, which contradicts the part-mark level and the requirement to draw a similarity.
P1 repeats its own part-credit rule in the point text ('Naming only the diets... gets part marks') as well as in the level, which is redundant.
P2's part-mark level rewards merely saying 'pythons are different', which is not a checkable idea and would credit an answer with no content.

The question requires support from the article, but no point says that the answer must use article evidence. P1 and P2 mix the pythons' adaptability with a restatement of the pandas' and koalas' limits, so one mistake could cost marks twice.
